walkthroughs.body_html:
Atomic Structure & Periodic Table — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atomic Structure & Periodic Table brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atomic Structure & Periodic Table.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which species has the same electron configuration as Ar?
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
F⁻
Mg²⁺

mcqs.q: Successive ionisation energies of an atom always:
options: Decrease
Stay the same
Increase
Vary randomly

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

mcqs.q: Why is the 4s orbital filled before the 3d orbital?
options: Because the 4s orbital has a lower energy than 3d when both are empty, so electrons fill it first.
Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
Because the 4s shell is closer to the nucleus than the 3d shell.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ionisation energy”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Isotope”?
options: Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Relative atomic mass”?
options: Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number Z”?
options: Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass number A”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Electron configuration”?
options: Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
